# A template is mutated once per type of dot, across the whole run.
#
# Two calls render "page" with the same Page, so the mutants and the
# verdicts would be identical the second time. The second subtree is
# trimmed instead, which is most of what makes a large template set
# affordable to mutate.
#
# -v says which subtrees were trimmed and where they were first reached,
# so a run that does less work than expected explains itself.

muxt test-template-mutations --dry-run -v --seed 1
cmp stdout want.txt

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- templates.gohtml --
{{define "page"}}<h1>{{.Title}}</h1>{{template "footer" .}}{{end}}
{{define "footer"}}<i>{{.Title}}</i>{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Page struct {
	Title string
}

func RenderHome(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "page", page)
}

func RenderArchive(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "page", page)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestHome(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := RenderHome(&buf, Page{Title: "hi"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "<h1>hi</h1><i>hi</i>"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("page = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
